## What it is

- A **shallow** snare: 13" across, 3" deep here (Wikipedia, "Snare drum": piccolo snares are 13-14" across and only about 4" or less tall, higher-pitched).

## How it sounds

- A drum head vibrates in **modes** at the zeros of the Bessel functions (Wikipedia, "Vibrations of a circular membrane"): not a harmonic series, which is why a drum has a pitch but no clear note. Hit the **centre** and mostly the round modes sound; hit the **edge** and many more ring.
- The **snares** (wires) lie on the bottom head and rattle when it moves; the **throw-off** lever lifts them off, and the drum sounds like a tom (Wikipedia, "Snare drum").
- Shallow shell: less body; tuned high: a "pop".

"Drum tuning." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_tuning). 14" snare batter 220-349 Hz, resonant head 330-391 Hz, most often a fifth above; bass drum front head port about 6", less "round"; muffling.

"Ludwig Drums." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Drums). Founded 1909; Ringo Starr on Ed Sullivan 1964; notable artists list (Al Jackson Jr., Clyde Stubblefield, Carlton Barrett, John Bonham, Joe Morello, Roger Taylor, Mick Fleetwood...).

"Snare drum." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snare_drum). Two heads, snares on the bottom head, a lever on the strainer throws them off (then it sounds like a tom); rimshots; kit snares 14" x 5-8"; piccolo 13-14" across, about 4" or less, higher.

"Vibrations of a circular membrane." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vibrations_of_a_circular_membrane). Modes of an ideal drum head at the zeros of the Bessel functions J_m.
:::
